analysis_notes.bechina_language_in_source_text: The word בְּחִינַת does not appear in the source text of Torah #87. However, the text uses two equivalent bechina markers extensively: (1) נִקְרָא ('is called') — used four times to equate concepts: יִרְאַת הָעֹנֶשׁ נִקְרָא צֶדֶק (line 3), יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת נִקְרָא אֱמוּנָה (line 3), יִרְאָה הַנִּקְרָא צֶדֶק (line 5), הַיִּרְאָה הַנִּקְרָא אֱמוּנָה (line 5), אַבְרָהָם נִקְרָא מִי שֶׁבָּא לְדַבֵּק (line 8); (2) הוּא ('is') — used once: יַעֲקֹב הוּא יִרְאָה (line 7). Per the framework (section 1.1), these are canonical bechina markers. All six of the above missing bechina connections should be added to the dataset.
analysis_notes.gap_analysis_conclusion: Torah #87 is a short, structurally tight teaching (9 lines) whose conceptual structure is almost entirely built from bechina equalities — but none of these bechina edges are yet in the dataset. The single existing edge (id 297, eitza) correctly captures the causal flow from יִרְאַת הָעֹנֶשׁ to אֱמוּנָה, but the six bechina equalities that form the teaching's scaffolding are missing. If those six edges were added, two connected components would emerge: (A) the fear-cluster with 5 nodes (יראת העונש, צדק, יראת הרוממות, אמונה, יעקב — and implicitly יראה as the general term linking them), and (B) the cleaving-cluster with 2 nodes (אברהם, דביקות). The causal flow from A to B (through אמונה leading to חסד/Abraham) would then be an eitza connecting the two packages.
